newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Mancera vows ongoing inflation fight.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Mancera vows ongoing inflation fight.

text.p: Banco de Mexico governor Miguel Mancera vowed on Saturday to continue to fight against inflation, saying lower inflation would help interest rates to fall.
"You can draw from this that we will continue giving our best effort so that inflation declines and from that, that interest rates can fall in a sustainable manner," Mancera said in a speech.
Mancera was speaking at the annual meeting of the Institute of Mexican Financial Executives.
He said that the government's inflation reduction policy had helped the economy grow by what he said should be about 4.5 percent this year.

That would be above the government's original estimate of about 3.0 growth for 1996. Other government officials have previously forecast that growth would be well above the originally announced 3.0 percent estimate.
"If it wasn't (the best policy), it would have been difficult for gross domestic product to be growing at a rate that in this year will reach about 4.5 percent, well above the goal," Mancera said.
He reiterated that inflation for the year is seen at above half of the level of 1995, when it reached close to 52 percent.
Mancera also noted that volatility in the peso exchange market had been sharply reduced recently, and said the peso now compares favourably the the German mark and the Japanese yen in its stability.
